title: Bidirectional A* vs Alfama Streets—Find Fast!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* race from start and goal across Alfama’s winding street graph. Each frame shows how two informed frontiers meet to cut search time while still guaranteeing an optimal route.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ **Bidirectional A*** is like having two smart navigators in Lisbon’s Alfama: one starts from your origin, the other from the destination—until they shake hands in the middle. 

🧠 **How it works (graph theory view):** We model the street network as a **weighted graph** (intersections = nodes, roads = edges). Then two **A*-guided** searches expand using an admissible heuristic, one forward and one backward, dramatically reducing the explored area compared to single-source search.

⚡ **Visualization insight:** Watch the frontier waves shrink as costs/heuristics steer both directions; when the explored regions intersect, we stitch together the best path from the meeting point—often achieving major speedups on real map-like graphs.

📍 Using real-world-style street connectivity, this reel turns route planning into a tangible **graph search** lesson.

👉 Want the next visualization for your city? Comment your neighborhood + route idea, and I’ll generate a fresh map-based demo!
fb_caption:
In this visualization, **Bidirectional A*** searches Alfama’s street graph from both the start and the goal at once. By treating the map as a weighted graph and using heuristic-guided expansion in two directions, the algorithm reduces unnecessary exploration and meets in the middle to reconstruct the optimal route.

If you enjoy learning with real map-style graphs, share this post with a friend who loves coding or shortest paths—and comment where you want the next city demo!
yt_description:
🚦 **Bidirectional A*** pathfinding on a real street-map graph in **Lisbon (Alfama)**!

In this YouTube Shorts reel, we visualize how two heuristic-guided searches run **from start and goal simultaneously**, shrinking the explored frontier until they meet. Learn the mechanics of graph search: intersections as nodes, roads as weighted edges, and A* using an admissible heuristic to efficiently find optimal routes.
